newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends at one year highs.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends at one year highs.

text.p: COMEX copper ended at a one-year high as continued strong fundamentals helped the market break through upside technical barriers to reach a firm footing at pre-Sumitomo price slide levels.
"A lot of the shorts won't be selling this market for a couple of days. I think it was a very positive close," John Tyree of FIMAT Futures said.
"We are reminded by the two-hour strike down at Enami that while there may not be anything definitive, there is always lurking in the background the possibility of further problems," Tyree added.
Workers at Enami, a copper smelting complex in Chile, walked out for two hours in protest at reported government plan to privatize the company.
COMEX July copper settled 2.00 cents firmer at 117.85 cents per pound, traded 118.20 to 114.60 cents. Volume was moderately heavy at an estimated 14,000 lots.
LME stocks fell 475 tonnes to 141,100 tonnes Tuesday, a small decrease compared to the recent trend of large, daily draws.
The LME cash to three months backwardation firmed some $20 Tuesday to $74/$79.
More analysts are predicting that the big copper surplus, which they had predicted would reach the market late 1996, will now be pushed back at least until next year.

Wiktor Bielski, senior commodities analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, told an industry conference Tuesday that copper prices were expected to remain high over the next 12 to 18 months with the market likely to be in deficit both this year and in 1998.
The market had consistently underestimated the strength of demand in recent years, Bielski said.
